report.hypothesisVerdict: Partly right: the script side was Bash, but the reason was Claude Code's permission system. The path was fixed in eb8f0f44 (27 May, "migrate agent personas to agentskills.io format"), and docs/agent-skills.md:14-44 records why. Allowlist rules compare literal command text. Bash never needed it: scripts/stack/run-stack.sh:4-5 finds its root from its own location. Later commits locked it in. 564e594b added the `make link` symlink. fcbadde9 denied `bash *`/`node *` and collapsed the allowlist onto the literal tools/** path. 7578ee29 made the canonical path a real clone. 4918fba0 gave tim a last-resort fallback to it. It also reads the same JIRA_*/SONAR_TOKEN variables, so nobody changes their setup. But the path stays fixed unless the plan also rewrites the model-typed layer: 18 allowlist lines (settings.json:63-93), about 1,000 mentions in 114 skill files plus 7 rules files, the workflow scripts (increment-build-loop.js:407, designer-prototyping-suite.js:45) and the 8 repo hook lines.

realBlockers.name: Stack ownership not enforced across clones (shared compose project name, stack commands that ignore the lease, lease ignores workspace)
realBlockers.why: Every clone drives the one `trade-imports` project (docker/stack/compose.yml:1). A plain `tim docker dev` writes no lease, and tim docker up/dev/down only refuse when a lease exists (tim/src/commands/docker/index.js:52-56). So clone B's up rebuilds clone A's containers from B's repos/ (dev.compose.yml ../../repos), and B's down runs `down --volumes` on A's data (stop-stack.sh:42). The lease records `workspace` (stack-lease.js:319) but nothing compares it, and the fixed holder 'perf' (lease.js:215) can be reused or released from another clone.
realBlockers.fix: Keep the single project name. Refuse when the running containers' com.docker.compose.project.working_dir label, or lease.workspace, is another clone, with --force to override. Also compare workspace in acquire and release.

realBlockers.name: tools/ bash scripts hardcode the canonical path (journey-builder worktrees and branches included)
realBlockers.why: About 130 tools scripts set WORKSPACE=$HOME/git/defra/trade-imports-workspace (for example prepare-digest.sh:16, style-add-item.sh:75, start-service-tag.sh:34). Run from clone 2, they read and write clone 1's workareas/ and repos/. journey-builder makes worktrees and spike/ and spec/ branches in clone 1 (prepare-digest.sh:52-54, :75-77).
realBlockers.fix: Find the root from BASH_SOURCE (with TIM_WORKSPACE as an override) right away, then port each folder to tim, which walks up from the current folder.
realBlockers.fixedBy: P02, P03 (then the per-folder ports; P63 retires journey-builder)

realBlockers.name: Globally linked tim runs one clone's code
realBlockers.why: `which tim` resolves through npm link to ~/git/defra/trade-imports-workspace/tim/src/cli.js, so clone 2 runs clone 1's tim code, node_modules and branch. Its auto-pull updates clone 2, but the code that runs is still clone 1's.
realBlockers.fix: The global tim becomes a launcher that hands over to the nearest clone's own tim/src/cli.js.

realBlockers.name: repos.json roster read from beside tim's code
realBlockers.why: tim/src/constants/repos.js:16-22,71 loads the first repos.json found (the one beside tim's code) once at module load, before --workspace is parsed, so clone 2 acts on its own folders with clone 1's repo list.
realBlockers.fix: Load the roster lazily from the resolved workspace root.

realBlockers.name: Build loop and prototype workflows resolve a fixed workspace
realBlockers.why: increment-build-loop.js:407-411 takes the first of three fixed candidates (clone 1 always wins) and has no override, so a loop launched from clone 2 builds, commits, takes the lease and runs `codex exec -C` in clone 1 (:3106). prepare-handoff.js:94, port-kit-page.js:77 and designer-prototyping-suite.js:44-45 (a literal /Users/samfarrington path) are fixed too.
realBlockers.fix: config.workspace as distil.js already does, otherwise resolve from the session folder or CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR.

realBlockers.name: Permission allowlist tied to the canonical path
realBlockers.why: 18 entries (.claude/settings.json:63-93) name ~/git/defra/trade-imports-workspace, so clone 2's own tools/ and repos/ commands prompt, while commands aimed at clone 1 are auto-allowed. The prefix rule at :84 also matches ...-workspace-2. Together with the skill text, this steers agents into clone 1.
realBlockers.fix: Prove which relative patterns match (with Sam watching), move script calls to Bash(tim:*), drop the canonical entries, and rewrite the skill text.

realBlockers.name: Local E2E from a clone that does not own the stack
realBlockers.why: The tests repo hard-codes localhost frontends (playwright.docker-compose.config.ts:10-13) and defaults the backend and Mongo URLs to localhost (:19-27). An E2E run from clone 2 silently tests clone 1's code and data, and nothing checks ownership.
realBlockers.fix: A Playwright globalSetup and the tim gate refuse unless this clone owns the stack (lease workspace or container label); ALLOW_FOREIGN_STACK=1 is the escape hatch.

realBlockers.name: Fit-test host ports 3050/3052/3053
realBlockers.why: Each frontend's test:fit:ci hard-codes PORT inline (package.json), and gates.json fixes the same ports. Two clones running the same frontend's fit rung at once: one is refused (gate.js:212-234). The rung needs no stack, so clones without one hit this.
realBlockers.fix: Use `PORT=${PORT:-N}` in each frontend, and have the gate move to the next free port.

realBlockers.name: Lease logs shared by every clone (minor)
realBlockers.why: logsDirFor defaults to ~/.local/state/tim/logs (lease.js:62-63) and runToLog truncates the file on each run (exec.js:84-88), so the last acquire or release from any clone replaces the previous log. Debug history only.

realBlockers.name: Plants prototype port 3103 (minor, run-time)
realBlockers.why: Two prototypes at once clash on 3103. The sign-in redirects, the session cookie and the Redis prefix also default to the same values (config.js:58-62, 224-235, 270-272, 302-306).
realBlockers.fix: Run the second one with PORT, DEFRA_ID_REDIRECT_URL, DEFRA_ID_SIGN_OUT_REDIRECT_URL, AUTH_SESSION_COOKIE_NAME and REDIS_KEY_PREFIX set. The Defra ID stub accepts any redirect URI, so it needs no change.

report.ciOnlyColleague: A colleague who never runs the stack needs only the path fixes, not the stack work. Once P01-P05 land, their clone can sit anywhere, run its own tim, and keep its own workareas/, branches and build-loop runs. They never take the stack lease, so P06 never refuses them. P07 stops them running local E2E against someone else's stack by accident. E2E comes from GitHub Actions: each service repo's PR calls the reusable e2e-tests.yml, which runs the suites and tags for that repo listed in config/e2e-tests-pr-scope.json. That is the evidence on their PR, and the build loop already waits on PR checks (wait-for-pr-checks.sh). The fit rungs and unit tests run natively with no stack. P08 lets their fit ports move if another clone on the same machine holds them. The one gap today: tim build gate's E2E rung needs the local stack, so a CI-only clone cannot pass the loop's gate. P10 adds an opt-in `--e2e ci` mode that leaves that rung to the PR's e2e check. What they lose: CI E2E follows the PR scope file, which can run less than the local gate, and each attempt waits a CI cycle. Their setup does not change otherwise: the same JIRA_USER, JIRA_TOKEN, JIRA_BASE_URL and SONAR_TOKEN in ~/.zshrc, and gh's own login.
